title: A set of nonzero acyclic dg submodules
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $\mathcal A$ be a sheaf dg $\mathcal O$-algebra. Use left sheaf dg modules and signed shifts as in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. There are a set $S$ and nonzero acyclic sheaf dg $\mathcal A$-modules $N_s$ for $s\in S$ such that every nonzero acyclic sheaf dg $\mathcal A$-module $M$ admits a monomorphism $N_s\hookrightarrow M$ for some $s\in S$. Here acyclic means that all underlying cohomology sheaves are zero; nonzero means that some graded component sheaf is nonzero.

source.place: Tag 0FST (lemma-small-acyclics), including the nonzero conclusion explicitly established in its proof, final paragraph. Left modules by the graded opposite algebra.

proof.text: On the open site, choose an infinite cardinal $\lambda$ bounding the number of opens and $\|\mathcal A\|$, and put $\mu=2^\lambda$. Here $\|E\|=|\coprod_{U,q}E^q(U)|$. These choices lie in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. The bijection between functions $\lambda\to\mathcal P(\lambda)$ and subsets of $\lambda\times\lambda$ gives $\mu^\lambda=\mu$. Fix a nonzero acyclic $M$ and choose $q,U$ and $0\ne x\in M^q(U)$, which exist by the stated meaning of nonzero. The zero subsheaf has size at most $\lambda$. Apply [lem-sfb-generated-sheaf-dg-submodule-size] with $F=0$ and the one section $x$ to obtain a dg subsheaf $F_0\subseteq M$ containing $x$ and of size at most $\mu$.

source.place: Tag 0FST (lemma-small-acyclics), proof, cardinal choice and nonzero seed paragraphs; use the corrected exponentiation-closed cardinal bound.

proof.text: Suppose $F_r\subseteq M$ is constructed with $\|F_r\|\leq\mu$. Its cycle triples $(V,j,z)$, $z\in F_r^j(V)$ and $dz=0$, form a set $L_r$ of size at most $\mu$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-cokernel-local-image] to the morphism of $\mathcal O$-module sheaves $d:M^{j-1}\to Z^j(M)=\ker(d:M^j\to M^{j+1})$. Its cokernel is $H^j(M)=0$, so its cokernel map is zero and its kernel is all of $Z^j(M)$. The cited statement therefore says precisely that every such $z$ is locally in the image of $d$: choose an open cover of $V$ and sections $w\in M^{j-1}$ on its members with $dw=z$ restricted there. Discard repeated opens, choosing one lift for each retained open. Each cover then has at most $\lambda$ members. Thus all chosen primitive triples form a set $K_r$ with $|K_r|\leq\mu\lambda=\mu$.

source.place: Tag 0FST (lemma-small-acyclics), proof, successor paragraph, choosing local primitives of every cycle; local-image criterion made explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-generated-sheaf-dg-submodule-size] to $F_r\subseteq M$ and the primitive sections indexed by $K_r$. It gives $F_{r+1}\subseteq M$ containing $F_r$ and those primitives, with $\|F_{r+1}\|\leq\mu$. Every cycle section of $F_r$ is now a boundary locally in $F_{r+1}$. Recursion on $r\in\mathbf N$, starting with step 1 and repeating steps 2--3, supplies an increasing sequence with both these properties. All stages contain the original nonzero section $x$.

source.place: Tag 0FST (lemma-small-acyclics), proof, successor construction and size induction.

proof.text: Let $K$ index all section triples of all $F_r$. Its cardinal is at most $\aleph_0\mu=\mu$. Apply [lem-sfb-generated-sheaf-dg-submodule-size] with $F=0$ and these sections to obtain $F_\infty\subseteq M$ of size at most $\mu$. The lemma's local formula shows that every section of $F_\infty$ locally belongs to some $F_r$: on each covering open only finitely many generators occur, so choose the largest of their finitely many stage indices; $F_r$ is closed under the action, differential and addition. Conversely every $F_r$ lies in $F_\infty$. If $z$ is a cycle section of $F_\infty$, these local representatives are cycles in $F_r$, because the inclusions into $M$ are sectionwise injective. Step 2 then supplies a further open cover on which each has a primitive in $F_{r+1}\subseteq F_\infty$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-cokernel-local-image], applied to $d:F_\infty^{j-1}\to Z^j(F_\infty)$, its cokernel map is zero: its kernel contains every local cycle section. That map is also an epimorphism by the cited statement, so the cokernel $H^j(F_\infty)$ is zero. This holds for every $j$. Finally $x\in F_\infty^q(U)$ remains nonzero. This argument uses the sheaf generated by the union, not a possibly nonsheaf sectionwise union.

source.place: Tag 0FST (lemma-small-acyclics), proof, final paragraph: sheaf union, nonzeroness, acyclicity and retained size bound, with local representatives written out.

proof.text: Here is the set assertion in the final paragraph, using the explicit dg data of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Fix a set $B$ of cardinality $\mu$. For each $(U,j)$ allow a carrier subset $C_{U,j}\subseteq B$. The tuples of these subsets form a set. For each tuple, the possible group operations, $\mathcal O(U)$-actions, restriction functions, differential functions and $\mathcal A^p(U)$-action functions form sets of functions between the indicated sets. Their products over all opens, inclusions and integer degrees are sets. Retain exactly the codes satisfying the sheaf, module, chain and dg identities, and then retain those defining nonzero acyclic objects. Call the resulting set $S$, and let $N_s$ be the coded sheaf dg module. Every dg module $E$ with $\|E\|\leq\mu$ has such a code: inject each section set into $B$ and transfer all functions along these bijections onto their images. The sheaf and dg equations are preserved, giving an isomorphism to a coded object. In particular steps 1--4 give, for any nonzero acyclic $M$, an isomorphism $N_s\cong F_\infty$ for some $s\in S$. Compose it with $F_\infty\hookrightarrow M$; the resulting dg map is sectionwise injective and therefore monic (cancellation is checked on sections). If there are no nonzero acyclic objects, $S$ may be empty and the assertion is vacuous.
